items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-09
items.q: And before Joe Oliver's time was Buddy Baldwin.

ctx.x: Do you think there are different kinds of jazz? He said he spoke about American jazz with his friends and German jazz.

Well, we don't look at it that way. I mean, when I play with them boys, they sound the same as anybody over here. I'm just saying that. And then... You mean the copy? How do we know who copy? Who we... Who, how... For generations, before my time was Joe Oliver. I was mine. Of course, there was other good ones, but I'm just narrating it down. And before Joe Oliver's time was Buddy Baldwin. Before Buddy Baldwin was an old man, so-and-so way back then, probably old man Merritt. That's generations. Now, how we know…
While you were down in Caracas, did you by any chance happen to get in personal contact with, uh, uh, some of our band leaders and musicians? I played on the TV there. Yeah.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Buddy Bowling just left when I was beginning to come out. Because he's the one that blew so loud, he blew himself crazy.

ctx.x: Louis, who would you say was the greatest influence on your life? Not in your youth, not musicians, I mean individuals. In your family or?

Well, my mother, she taught us the real things. She always said, you probably never get rich. She was wrong there, wasn't she? Well, she might be. Maybe, you know, maybe $10 million to save $10, you know. But I mean, what she means were have yachts and still got a zillion. We wasn't even thinking about that. She wasn't even thinking about it when she told me, say, but you'll always have health. So take a laxative every night of your life. And that's the finest things you ever told me. You didn't have much money…
When did you leave New Orleans?
